In-window: the Oct-28 FOMC, late-October hyperscaler capex prints (sector beta), and a possible PR on first Barber Lake hall delivery or rent start, which the 8-K guides only to 'Q4 2026' [4]. I no longer tilt for the Oct-23 V3/Bitfury tranche: the Form 4 footnotes show it settles a prepaid variable forward struck and hedged in Nov-2025, so it is not new supply [5]. fair_value.method: 12m-forward blend of a site-level split-rate DCF ($6.56, 55%) and a split-cap NAV ($8.64, 45%). Every site appears once: three leases at contract terms, Odessa as mining or HPC conversion (mutually exclusive), 10 pipeline sites probability-weighted net of capex ($0.85B, Colchis at 76%), WindHQ sold (Canaan shares $18M credited). Net debt $5.15B, 500M shares. A single 9% rate gives a DCF of $5.33.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-level split-rate DCF (12m-forward). Single 9% rate on the same cash flows: EV $6.55B -> $5.33. Contracted-only: $4.58 split / $3.35 single. GPU life: 4y $6.09, 7y $7.02.

A sustained close below it would most likely mean the market is impairing the signed leases themselves, not just pricing the pipeline out: Fluidstack stress beyond the ~45% Google backstop, Barber Lake delays or overruns beyond $359.3M, a forced parent raise, or covenant pressure. $7.0 now sits within 7% of my $7.50 fair value, so ordinary volatility could reach it.

reasoning: Round 4: site-by-site coverage and split-rate discounting. (1) I rebuilt contracted cash flows from each lease's terms (inventory figures) instead of the stale Q2-26 deck schedule. Black Pearl: 216 IT MW, $296M yr-1, 3%, hall-by-hall 15 yrs. Stingray: AWS (not Fluidstack, round-3 error), 70 MW, $108M from May-27. Barber Lake: 207 IT MW (not 244), $3.8B Fluidstack term (not $3B), then the $5.2B AI-lab follow-on with a 12.5% haircut. The site-level path ($702M in 2028 vs the deck's $727M) is slightly below the company's. (2) Per the round-3 supervisor, the 8.5% exit cap on 2037 NOI is replaced by explicit expiries with 75% renewal at 85% rent, refit capex, and an 8.5% cap on post-renewal NOI. The Fluidstack refresh-default term is rescaled to Barber Lake's ~44% share. (3) Split discounting: AWS term 6.5% (anchored on the 6.0-6.125% Ba2 secured notes against AA-guaranteed leases), Fluidstack term 7.5% (7.125% Ba3 notes plus tenor), AI lab 8.5%, overhead 7.0%, everything post-contract at the 9% WACC. DCF: split $6.56, single-rate $5.33 (round 3 $7.20 single). The drop at a single rate comes from the expiry-based terminal plus overhead carried through it (~-$1.1), the follow-on haircut (~-$0.3) and lower site NOI (~-$0.4), partly offset by site-level pipeline, mining and Canaan. (4) Every inventory site appears once. The pipeline is valued site by site, net of capex and concessions, at stated probabilities: $0.85B incl. Apollo, Milsing and both expansions (previously ~0), with Colchis at 76%. Odessa is mining ($33M) or HPC conversion (40%), never both. WindHQ is excluded and its Canaan shares are credited ($18M). NAV with split caps: $8.64. Fair value $8.05 -> $7.50. Ladder: the scenarios shift down modestly (bear $6.2/31%, base $12.3/48%, bull $25.5/21%), P(>= spot) 0.355 -> 0.34. The 1-month ladder is unchanged: nothing in this round moves a 1-month horizon. Thesis break $7.0 -> $6.5. Research this round: one data lookup (Canaan quote); the rest came from the inventory and filings already cited.

Fluidstack term (Barber Lake 2027-36; unrated tenant, ~45% Google Aa2 backstop): 7.5% = Cipher Compute 7.125% notes (Ba3/BB-) + ~40bp tenor, with the refresh default as an explicit cash-flow loss. AI-lab follow-on 2037-46 (unnamed, unrated, no backstop, no debt priced): 8.5% plus a 12.5% expected-loss haircut. Corporate overhead at 7.0% (blended contracted rate) in the split case. Post-contract renewal, terminal, pipeline and mining at the 9.0% WACC. Single-rate case: everything at 9.0%.
